speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with confusion, abdominal pain, and vomiting; to begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any fever or changes in your urine color?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old female. The patient presents to the emergency department with confusion that started this morning. The patient's husband reports that she initially complained of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fatigue after eating and has vomited 3 times. The patient has progressively become more confused throughout the day. The patient's past medical history includes morbid obesity, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, a sleeve gastrectomy 1 month ago, and depression with multiple suicide attempts.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) precipitated by gastric stasis post-sleeve gastrectomy. The combination of recent bariatric surgery, vomiting, abdominal pain, and new-onset confusion in a diabetic patient is highly suggestive of metabolic derangement. Have you taken any of your diabetes medications today?
